name: AZ-09
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Paul Gosar running for reelection with cash advantage
Markets price Gosar at ~94% to win
No public polling of the race
model.rationale: The R+15 district lean, Gosar's incumbency and fundraising edge, and Polymarket pricing near 94% for Republicans all point the same way, with no polling or ratings suggesting a competitive race. The forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based margin of roughly fifteen points Republican.
model.watch: A major scandal or unexpected outside spending surge against Gosar would be the main thing to move this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Paul Gosar seeks another term in a northeastern Arizona district that leans about fifteen points Republican, giving Democrats little structural opening. Gosar holds a clear financial advantage, with roughly $303,000 on hand compared with about $26,000 for Democrat Dani Sterbinsky, who has raised a modest sum for a challenge of this scale. No outside groups have invested meaningfully in the race on either side.

Prediction markets put Gosar's chances around 94 percent, and no public polls or expert ratings indicate the seat is in play. The forecast expects a Republican win by roughly fifteen points, with modest uncertainty given the absence of polling.
